title: NIST AI RMF 1.0 to ISO/IEC 42001:2023

useCase.intendedUsers: Lead auditors and reviewers who want to show where evidence gathered against one framework also bears on the other.
useCase.purpose: Show where ISO/IEC 42001 audit evidence also bears on NIST AI RMF outcomes, and the reverse.
useCase.assumptions: Relationships compare what each requirement asks for, not how an organisation implements it. Each entry is single-source, so it can be read in both directions. No inference may be drawn from outcomes or requirements that are not mapped. Every entry is intersects_with: a NIST outcome and the other requirement only overlap, so a full result on one side is never shown as full on the other. The NIST side was read against NIST AI 100-1 Tables 1 to 4 (checked 2026-11-13). Draft until the ISO/IEC 42001 framework is released (#57): its numbers are not yet confirmed against a licensed copy, and the titles on that side are our own.

entries.justification: Understanding legal and regulatory requirements overlaps with determining the relevant requirements of interested parties, which include legal ones.
Building trustworthy characteristics into policies overlaps with the AI policy set by top management; neither prescribes the other's content.
Setting the level of risk management from risk tolerance overlaps with planning for AI risks and opportunities, including risk criteria.
Establishing the risk management process through policies and controls overlaps with establishing and maintaining the management system.
Planned monitoring and review of the risk process overlap with monitoring and measuring management system performance.
Periodic review of risk management outcomes overlaps with management review at planned intervals.
An inventory of AI systems overlaps with recording the resources each AI system depends on; the inventory itself is not that control's aim.
Documented roles and responsibilities for AI risk work overlap with assigning responsibilities and authorities for the management system.
Documented roles for mapping, measuring and managing AI risks overlap with defining and allocating AI roles.
Training to perform AI risk duties overlaps with ensuring the competence of people doing AI-related work.
Executive responsibility for AI risk decisions overlaps with top management commitment to the management system.
Practices that enable incident identification overlap with letting people raise concerns about AI systems.
Collecting external feedback on impacts overlaps with letting outside parties report adverse impacts.
Policies for third-party AI risks overlap with supplier arrangements for AI.
Documenting intended purposes and context overlaps with determining the organisation's context and issues relevant to AI; MAP 1.1 works per system.
Documenting risk tolerances overlaps with the risk criteria set when planning for AI risks.
Eliciting system requirements overlaps with stating what the AI system must do.
TEVV considerations on data selection overlap with requirements for data to be fit for use.
Characterising the likelihood and magnitude of impacts overlaps with planning AI system impact assessments.
Characterising impacts on individuals and groups overlaps with assessing effects on individuals and groups of people.
Involving independent assessors overlaps with internal audits of the management system, which concern the system, not each AI system.
Documenting test sets, metrics and tools overlaps with verifying and validating the AI system against its requirements.
Monitoring behaviour in production overlaps with operating and monitoring the AI system in use.
Tracking existing and emergent risks regularly overlaps with performing AI risk assessments at planned intervals and on change.
Planning responses to high-priority risks overlaps with planning AI risk treatment.
Documented responses to high-priority risks overlap with implementing the AI risk treatment plan.
Monitoring third-party risks and controls overlaps with supplier arrangements for AI.
Post-deployment monitoring plans overlap with operating and monitoring the AI system in use.
Continual improvement built into system updates overlaps with continual improvement of the management system.
Communicating incidents to relevant actors overlaps with telling users about incidents.

notes: Only the strongest direct overlaps are recorded; an outcome without an entry is unmapped, not a gap. The ISO/IEC 42001 side is cited by clause number only (D-03): no text of the standard is used. NIST publishes its own informative crosswalk on the AI Resource Center; it was not used, and this mapping is not an official one.
